scope: Complete curriculum objectives and exemplar range; current-body serving approvals remain separate.

rows.objective: A fraction as part of a whole
rows.constraints: denominators 2-12
hints: What does the denominator count, and what does the numerator count in this representation?
Identify equal parts or equal members of the set before counting the selected ones.
Check whether the fraction describes less than, equal to, or more than one whole as requested.

rows.constraints: whole numbers up to 30; do not require simplifying
hints: Count the selected objects; that count will be the numerator.
Count every object in the set; that total will be the denominator.
Write selected over total, then verify that the denominator counts every object exactly once.

rows.objective: Comparing simple fractions and the whole
rows.constraints: unit fractions or the whole; denominators 2-10
hints: First decide whether one choice is the whole number 1; every proper unit fraction is less than one whole.
If both choices are unit fractions of equal wholes, the smaller denominator makes each one-part piece larger.
Use the whole-number comparison or the denominator comparison that fits the choices, then check each fraction has numerator one.

rows.constraints: denominators 2-10, fractions between 0 and 1
hints: How many equal intervals make one whole on this number line?
Count those intervals from zero, continuing past one whole when the numerator requires it.
Check the location by writing the number of intervals over the intervals per whole.

rows.constraints: improper fractions with denominators 2-6
hints: Mark the denominator number of equal intervals from one whole-number tick to the next.
Starting at zero, count the numerator as a count of intervals, with each interval sized one over the denominator.
Group complete denominator-sized sets of intervals to place the tick between its consecutive whole numbers.

rows.constraints: denominators 2-10
hints: Each step measures one divided by the given denominator. How many steps span a whole-number interval?
Multiply the whole-number coordinate by that denominator to count its intervals from zero.
Put that interval count over the given denominator and verify the division returns the original whole number.

rows.constraints: target denominator is a small multiple of the original
hints: Divide the target denominator by the original denominator to find the scale factor.
Multiply the original numerator by that same scale factor.
Check that multiplying both numerator and denominator by the factor gives the target denominator without changing the fraction.

rows.constraints: numerator and denominator up to 30
hints: Find the greatest common factor shared by the numerator and denominator.
Divide both numerator and denominator by that greatest common factor.
Verify the new numerator and denominator have no common factor greater than one.

rows.constraints: values up to 60
hints: Find a common factor of the numerator and denominator and divide both by it to obtain a simpler equivalent fraction.
Repeat the common-factor check until each fraction is in lowest terms, or rewrite both fractions with a shared denominator.
Compare the reduced values by their numerators over a common denominator, and check cross-products agree with the comparison.

rows.constraints: denominators up to 12
hints: Check whether the two fractions have equal denominators or equal numerators.
With equal denominators compare numerators; with equal numerators, the smaller denominator names the larger piece.
Choose the requested smaller or larger fraction and verify the comparison using the matching equality.

rows.constraints: unlike denominators up to 12
hints: Find a common denominator that both original denominators divide into.
Multiply each numerator and denominator by the factor needed to reach that common denominator.
Compare the resulting numerators and verify each rewritten fraction has the same value as its original.

rows.constraints: 3 fractions or a benchmark of 1/2 or 1
hints: Compare each fraction with the stated benchmark, such as one half or one whole, before ordering.
Use the benchmark results to place fractions below, equal to, or above it, then compare any remaining close pair directly.
Write every requested fraction in order and verify each adjacent pair has the required smaller-to-larger relation.

rows.constraints: same denominator up to 12; sum less than 1, no simplifying needed
hints: Keep the common denominator because the parts already have the same size.
Add the numerators to count how many of those equal parts there are.
Check the new numerator is smaller than the denominator, confirming the sum stays below one.

rows.constraints: same denominator up to 12; simplify the result
hints: Keep the shared denominator and subtract the second numerator from the first numerator.
Write that difference over the unchanged denominator.
Find any common factor of the new numerator and denominator and divide both by it to verify lowest terms.

rows.constraints: same denominator; results may exceed 1, give lowest terms
hints: Keep the common denominator and add all numerators.
Reduce numerator and denominator by their greatest common factor.
If total exceeds one, write the requested mixed form.

rows.constraints: one denominator a multiple of the other, up to 12
hints: Use the denominator that is a multiple of the smaller denominator.
Scale numerator and denominator to it, then combine numerators.
Verify both rewritten fractions share the denominator.

rows.constraints: denominators up to 12, unlike
hints: Find the least common denominator.
Make equivalent fractions and add or subtract numerators.
Reduce by the greatest common factor.

rows.objective: Sums greater than one and three fractions
rows.constraints: denominators up to 12; results may exceed 1
hints: Choose one common denominator for every addend.
Rewrite every addend and combine all numerators.
Reduce the total and convert if requested.

rows.constraints: denominator divides the whole number evenly
hints: What equal share is one denominator-part of the whole quantity?
Divide the whole by the denominator, then take the requested number of those shares.
Check that the selected quantity is sensible for the stated fraction and context.

rows.constraints: denominator divides the whole number; numerator 2-9
hints: Divide the whole by the denominator for one equal share.
Multiply that share by the numerator.
Verify the result divided by numerator gives one share.

rows.objective: Fraction of a quantity in context
rows.constraints: whole-number answers; quantities up to 60
hints: What equal share is one denominator-part of the whole quantity?
Divide the whole by the denominator, then take the requested number of those shares.
Check that the selected quantity is sensible for the stated fraction and context.

rows.constraints: numerators and denominators up to 9; result already in lowest terms
hints: Multiply numerator by numerator.
Multiply denominator by denominator.
Reduce only if finished terms share a factor.

rows.constraints: result reducible; values up to 12
hints: Identify genuine cross numerator-denominator factors.
Cancel them first or multiply across before reducing.
Verify reduced and unreduced products are equivalent.

rows.constraints: cancel common factors before multiplying; values up to 12
hints: Write a whole number as that number over one.
Cancel only matching cross factors.
Multiply remaining factors and verify lowest terms.

root_delta_review: The step length one divided by the denominator partitions a whole into denominator-many steps; wording avoids asserting the classification answer while retaining the precise partition method. Other rows unchanged from independently accepted input.
